The actions described in the paragraph do not appear to violate standard legal labor standards, provided that the employees are compensated for the additional hours worked in accordance with applicable overtime laws. The text states that employees were already working the "maximum hours permitted by local labor laws," which implies that any additional hours worked during the extended retail hours would likely constitute overtime. Most labor laws require that hours worked beyond a standard workweek (or daily limit, depending on jurisdiction) be paid at a higher rate (e.g., time-and-a-half). The phrase "without increasing pay" is ambiguous; if it means no increase in hourly wage rate, that is standard unless overtime applies. If it means no additional compensation whatsoever for the extra hours, that would likely be illegal. However, since the text says they were *already* at the maximum permitted hours, working *more* hours would inherently trigger overtime pay requirements in most jurisdictions. If "without increasing pay" means they are not receiving overtime premiums, this would be a violation. If it simply means their base hourly rate isn't changing, that is compliant. Given the ambiguity, the most likely legal interpretation is that if they are not receiving overtime pay for the extra hours, it is non-compliant. If they are receiving overtime pay, it is compliant. The text does not explicitly state whether overtime pay was provided, only that pay wasn't "increased" (which could mean base rate). Assuming standard labor laws require overtime pay for hours worked beyond the maximum permitted, and the store extended hours *beyond* that maximum, the employees are working illegal hours unless compensated as overtime. The key legal issue is whether the "maximum hours permitted" refers to a daily or weekly cap that was already hit. If they hit the cap, they cannot legally work more without overtime pay. If the store did not provide overtime pay, it is illegal. The text says "without increasing pay," which strongly suggests no additional compensation was given for the extra hours, implying a likely violation of overtime laws.
